I used Mint for about a year before finally switching to Solus... I use Budgie. It's a great system and pretty-much built from the ground-up; it's not even really Linux, from what I (not a coder or anything) understand.
Solus mentions Linux on the about and "technologies" pages.
I've used Ubuntu, Kubuntu, Xubuntu, PopOS, and Fedora… I always end up coming back to Mint with xfce.

My next upgrade (whenever that is, I need to see what Mint does about the rise of SNAPs), will probably be using MATE. XFCE, in the past few years, seems to come up with more and more bugs and minor issues, I think it has to do with the adjustment to GTK3
Mint is a great place to start, and to stick with. I used Ubuntu for years. Currently, I am using Manjaro for my day to day.
Just make sure to use xfce and not the bloatfest desktop management systems.
Actually, MATE is actually less bloated than XFCE in many ways now. But yeah, forget about Cinnamon.

It's what I started with and it's good, but there were a couple reasons why I switched:

  • switching between releases is slightly annoying
  • packages in the mint repositories are sometimes outdated, if you you want a newer one, you need to add a PPA... not great
  • Getting graphics card switching on a laptop with an Nvidia GPU was poorly explained/outdated (had to resort to ArchWiki to actually find out what to do)

This is when I realized that I wanted a rolling release distro (no major upgrades, always just a newest version) and no more hand holding. So I installed Arch. It's not as difficult as people think, just a little tedious and a lot to learn in the beginning, but the ArchWik a great knowledge source and makes it all worth it. I had my installation all decked out, everything was perfect, then my HDD died. I replaced it with an SSD, got lazy, put Manjaro on it (easy version of Arch) and stuck with that for now. It's not perfect either, but all Linux distros have their peculiarities. You learn to deal with it...
